summary: Fixed the last unjustified compile refusal. Root cause (reproduced at ops/suite/dev/chunk_generalized_iplr_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_o.py:76:394): the kernel's dispatch idiom reads b_Aqk.to(b_v.dtype).shape[1], which is constexpr in the pinned source language (the inline cast result's TYPE and SHAPE are trace-time tensor metadata), but ConstexprEnv could not fold the inline value-method call, so the IfExp condition stayed runtime, BOTH arms were lowered, and the dead else arm's fp64 dot (fp64 pointers: the float32-labeled case layer hands numpy-default float64 buffers) refused. Fix in a100c/frontend/specialize.py: _fold_cast_method folds X.to(D)/X.cast(D) over a runtime symbol to the cast RESULT's RuntimeValue (target type, receiver's shape) -- metadata only, never a value; .shape/.dtype and every dtype predicate on the cast result then fold, dead dispatch arms are never lowered, and statement-level if and IfExp both consume the fold. The operator's 3 identities now compile (2 shapes of one identity share one artifact, cache hit); all 6 declared cases execute and compare PASS under their declared policies at 1 and 4 workers. The fp64-dot refusal justification was updated on FRONTEND_COVERAGE.json's tl.dot row: no genuinely-fp64 form remains (a live fp64-dot probe keeps the located boundary refusal; the corpus declares no float64). New regression test a100c/tests/test_t040_repairs.py covers .to(x.dtype) and x.dtype-dependent constexpr arithmetic for a block whose dtype comes from each of the 8 corpus dtypes, with no-baking (two dtype identities -> two artifacts; two runtime shapes -> one), a genuinely-fp64 boundary witness, and a fold-disabled control that reproduces the pre-fix refusal. t036/t038 boundary expectations updated to the repaired reality. The affected class (the 9 corpus operators using the inline .to(...).shape dispatch idiom) was rerun end to end: 53/57 cases PASS; the 4 non-PASS rows are two PRE-EXISTING defects, proven fold-independent by byte-identical artifacts with the fold disabled (see remaining_work). Full test suite: 45/45 files pass.

evidence: The load-bearing control is in a100c/tests/test_t040_repairs.py::check_fold_disabled_control: with ConstexprEnv._fold_cast_method disabled, the operator's float32-labeled case refuses again with the exact pre-fix signature (tl.dot: fp64 tl.dot is outside the corpus dtype surface, line 76) and the probe's dead arm is lowered again -- proving the passing checks are not vacuous. The executed comparisons: run_scan at 1 and 4 workers, 6/6 declared cases PASS each under the case's own allclose policy; the fold records show b_Aqk.to(b_v.dtype).shape[1] < 16 evaluated and recorded True for every identity (the folded comparison is still evaluated, never skipped); the TIR contains only fp32 linalg.dot ops. No baking: the sweep's repeat-case checks and the test's identity/artifact split (fp32 vs fp16 differ, n=8 vs n=64 share) both hold. Fold inertness outside the idiom: byte-identical artifacts with the fold on/off for gdn2 and 6 out-of-class operators.
remaining_work: PRE-EXISTING (proven fold-independent, byte-identical artifacts with the fold disabled): chunk_gdn2_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused bakes a case-tier launch geometry into a shape-independent cache key. Reproduction: compile the [17] and [3,17,2,7] float32 payloads in separate fresh processes -- both produce cache key 020c5b09... but different executables (sha 44bfa945 vs 48929706); the [17]-compiled artifact leaves (b,h)-blocks >= 4 uncomputed at [3,17,2,7] (Akk output 0.0 vs reference 1.0, first bad flat indices 1088/1104/...). stage.plan.txt diff shows the cause: for the [17] case the grid axis folds to the constant 4 (the case-layer literal B=2, H=2 of the (17,)-shape builder is not identity-stable: the same identity's [3,17,2,7,6] case has B=3), while the [3,17,2,7] compile correctly ties the axis to ($bundle_view('Akkd',0) mul $bundle_view('Akkd',2)). A follow-up task should stop the grid model folding case-tier literals that are not identity-stable across the SHAPES table (or key the artifact on them).

PRE-EXISTING harness defect (independent of the compiler): tools/run_scan.py's resource-evidence capture passes a counts.json path containing the case id (shape lists with commas) through QEMU's '-plugin file,out=PATH' argument, which QEMU splits on commas -- the plugin writes to a truncated path and the driver raises FileNotFoundError, so resource-flagged multi-dim-shape cases (e.g. chunk_abc [2,2,17,9,8,4]#float16, the dev representative) record LAUNCH_FAIL. Direct QEMU probe confirms (a file named 'suite__dev__op.py#[2' is created). The same case's plain execution passes. Fix: a comma-free evidence path (or escaping) in capture_resource_evidence.
